newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Jan 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Jan 28.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Tuesday:
* Hilton Hotels makes an unsolicited bid for ITT Corp, the owner of the Sheraton hotel chain, for $55 per ITT share, or about $6.5 billion, and the assumption of $4 billion in debt.
* General Motors increases its dividend to $0.50 a share and announces plans to buy back $2.5 billion worth of its stock in the next 12 months.
* American Express says it will cut about 3,300 jobs, or about 4.6 percent, of its work force.
* Honeywell says it will buy Measurex Corp for $600 million, making Honeywell the leading seller of controls and services for pulp and paper plants.
* CVS says it is in talks to acquire Revco D.S. Inc in a deal that would make CVS the second largest drugstore company.
* National Semiconductor agrees to sell a majority stake in Fairchild Semiconductor for $550 million.
* Tower Automotive agress to acquire an auto component supply unit of A.O. Smith for $625 million.
* Mobil reports fourth quarter earnings above Wall Street estimates, but ARCO's results come in below analysts' forecasts.
* The Dow Jones industrials falls 35.79 points to close at 6,660.69.
* Sales of existing homes fell 3.5 percent in December but set a record for the year by rising above four million.
* Volvo Chief Executive Soeren Gyll quits a year earlier than expected.
* Moves by Swiss courts to hand over confidential banking documents to the Indian Government revives a scandal over alleged bribes paid by Swedish arms company Bofors.
* AT&T announces plans to offer local phone service in California starting February 3.

* The World Economic Forum, to be held in Davos, Switzerland starting January 30, and smaller forums across the world gain popularity among those willing to pay high prices to meet political and corporate leaders.
* Index funds gain popularity in the bull market.
* Development in Atlantic City cools and the future of the city's casino industry faces new hurdles.
* President Clinton will soon ask Congress to give a tax credit to businesses that hire welfare recipients.
